items.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009
items.q: Willie Humphrey would have been the last and he passed away just months before my arrival to the city.

ctx.x: This New Orleans clarinet tradition. I would have to guess this was not something that you sat down and said where’s a niche for me, and then recognized this niche and pursued it.

No the niche revealed itself. The niche revealed itself. Because you have to remember, Monk, when I actually moved to New Orleans in 1994, there were no clarinetists left for me to study with directly. Willie Humphrey would have been the last and he passed away just months before my arrival to the city. So it’s not that the style revealed itself to me as my niche, it’s just that I kept finding it strange that the only clarinetists that I enjoy were gone, were in recordings, I mean in New Orleans proper. And of…
even when I first moved to New Orleans there was a lot of vocabulary I didn’t — that had captured my ear enough to check it out, but I hadn’t really incorporated it.
